title: "How to read a public budget" companion (neutral fiscal literacy)
context: Many readers of budget explainers benefit from a brief companion document explaining general public-budget concepts: fund accounting, the difference between budgeted and actual figures, fiscal years, nominal versus real, and how to navigate a government budget document. This is a neutral, educational, product-neutral companion — it does not advise on policy choices, advocate any position, or provide financial/legal advice. It is a backlog item for after the pilot explainers are stable.
objective: Write a neutral, plain-language 'how to read a public budget' companion document that explains key public-budget concepts (fund accounting, budgeted vs actual, fiscal years, nominal vs real) in a product-neutral, non-advisory, non-advocacy way.
acceptanceCriteria: Explains key public-budget concepts: fund accounting, budgeted vs actual vs adjusted, fiscal years, nominal vs real (with a named example of how deflators work), and how to navigate a government budget document
Strictly neutral and educational: product-neutral, no advocacy, no advice, no calls-to-action, no policy recommendations
Not financial, legal, or investment advice of any kind; clearly labeled as educational context
Plain-language reading-level appropriate for a general resident audience
Reviewed and signed off by the maintainer; neutral reviewer review recommended
output: A neutral, plain-language 'how to read a public budget' companion document covering key public-finance concepts — educational, product-neutral, non-advisory, accessible, and CC-BY-4.0 licensed.
